p1.title: Orient and navigate
p1.can_do: You can get into MESA, find data, run an app, and keep what you make.
p1.reflection: What would you do first if a file you saved was not where you expected it?

p2.title: Run and understand
p2.can_do: You can say what a dataset holds and where it is incomplete or doubtful, before you compute with it.
p2.reflection: What would you check first if this result looked wrong?

p3.title: Query and connect
p3.can_do: You can ask questions across files and tables, and show that combining them did what you meant.
p3.reflection: After combining two tables, what tells you that nothing was added or lost?

p4.title: Explore and verify
p4.can_do: You can work with an AI assistant and test what it tells you against the data.
p4.reflection: What would make you trust, or not trust, an answer an AI assistant gave you?

p5.title: Preserve and share
p5.can_do: You can leave work that someone else can find, understand, and run again.
p5.reflection: What would someone else need from you to run this again without asking you?

last-row.ask: Show the last row of `readings`. Which gauge and day is it?
last-row.right: The file runs gauge by gauge, so it ends with G05 on the last day of July.

slips.G01, 2026-07-01: That is the first row, which `head()` shows. `tail()` shows the end.

last-row.otherwise: Run `readings.tail(1)` and read the `gauge_id` and `date` columns.

g02-in-millimetres.ask: The largest reading at G02 is 2.92. What is it in millimetres?
g02-in-millimetres.right: G02 reports in centimetres, and a centimetre is ten millimetres.

slips.2.92: That is the value as stored, in centimetres. It has not been converted.
slips.0.292: That divides by ten. Centimetres to millimetres multiplies by ten.

g02-in-millimetres.otherwise: Find G02's unit in `gauges`, then convert 2.92 to millimetres.

zero-readings.ask: How many readings have a `value` of exactly 0?
zero-readings.right: More than half of the 152 readings are dry days.

slips.150: That is the number of blank flags. The question is about `value`.
slips.0: No `value` is blank, but 80 of them are zero. A zero is a measurement, not a gap.

zero-readings.otherwise: Compare `value` with 0 and add up the matches.

largest-unflagged.ask: Leave out the flagged readings. What is the largest `value` that remains?
largest-unflagged.right: Without the suspect reading of 180, the largest is an ordinary wet day at G03.

slips.180: The flagged reading is still in. Keep only the rows whose flag is not `S`.
slips.2.92: That is the largest at G02 alone.

largest-unflagged.otherwise: Keep the rows whose flag is not `S`, then take the largest `value`.

rows-without-repeats.ask: Remove exact repeats with `drop_duplicates()`. How many rows remain?
rows-without-repeats.right: One row, G03 on 5 July, is written twice, so 152 becomes 151.

slips.152: That is the table as loaded. One row for G03 is written twice.
slips.155: That is a complete table, 5 gauges for 31 days. This one has four missing days as well as a repeat.
slips.1: That is how many rows are removed, not how many remain.

rainy-local-days.ask: In local time, on how many days of the week did rain fall at G03?
rainy-local-days.right: Two of the seven local days were dry.

slips.6: That counts UTC dates. Evening rain crosses midnight UTC, so it spills into an extra date.
slips.7: That counts every day of the week. Two had no rain.
slips.8: That is the number of UTC dates the week touches, wet or dry.

rainy-local-days.otherwise: Convert to local time, total the rain for each local day, and count the totals above 0.

rainy-hours.ask: In how many of the 168 hours is `rain_mm` above 0?
rainy-hours.right: Rain fell in about one hour in ten.

slips.168: That is every hour. Most of them are dry.
slips.336: That is every row of the long table, both measurements together.

rainy-hours.otherwise: In the reshaped table, compare `rain_mm` with 0 and add up the matches.

rows-in-centimetres.ask: After the join, how many rows have a `unit` of `cm`?
rows-in-centimetres.right: Only G02 reports in centimetres, and it has 31 readings.

slips.1: That counts gauges. The join gives every one of G02's readings its unit.
slips.121: Those are the rows in millimetres.

rows-in-centimetres.otherwise: Count the rows of `joined` whose `unit` is `cm`.

verify.python:
joined = readings.merge(gauges, on="gauge_id", how="left", validate="many_to_one")
int((joined["unit"] == "cm").sum())

readings-above-twenty.ask: With one SQL query on `readings.parquet`, count the readings above 20.
readings-above-twenty.right: The count mixes units, as the file does, so G02's centimetre values never pass 20.

slips.152: That is every row. Add `WHERE value > 20`.

wettest-after-cleaning.ask: Convert G02 to millimetres, leave out the flagged readings, and drop the repeated row. Which gauge then has the largest July total?
wettest-after-cleaning.right: Observatory leads once the data is cleaned. G01 is still missing four days, so even this is not yet a fair comparison.

slips.G05, 390.9 mm: That total includes the reading of 180 that the sensor flagged as suspect.
slips.G05, 210.9 mm: That is G05 without its flagged reading, but G03 is higher.
slips.G03, 273.6 mm: The repeated row for 5 July is still counted twice.

wettest-after-cleaning.otherwise: Apply all three steps, then total by gauge.

verify.python:
clean = readings.merge(gauges, on="gauge_id", validate="many_to_one")
clean["mm"] = clean["value"].where(clean["unit"] == "mm", clean["value"] * 10)
clean = clean[clean["flag"] != "S"].drop_duplicates(subset=["gauge_id", "date"])
totals = clean.groupby("gauge_id")["mm"].sum().round(1)
f"{totals.idxmax()}, {totals.max()} mm"

missing-flags-in-r.right: All but two readings have a blank flag, and `na.strings = ""` reads a blank as missing.

slips.0: The file was read without `na.strings = ""`, so blanks are empty text, not missing values.
slips.2: Those are the flagged readings. `is.na()` counts the ones with no flag.

missing-flags-in-r.otherwise: Read the file with `na.strings = ""`, then run the line.

northernmost-gauge.right: Observatory has the largest latitude, so it sits at the top of the map.

slips.G05, Quarry: Quarry has the smallest latitude. It is furthest south.
slips.G01, Boathouse: Boathouse is furthest west. Its longitude is the most negative.

northernmost-gauge.otherwise: North is up on the map, and larger latitude is further north.

shared-or-community.ask: The path you copied stops at `/iplant/home/shared`, and the listing holds many projects that are not MESA's. Which did you click?
shared-or-community.right: Shared opens every CyVerse community project. Community is the MESA folder inside it.

slips.Community: Community opens the MESA folder, and its path goes on to `/iplant/home/shared/mesa`.

shared-or-community.otherwise: Look at where the path ends. The MESA folder's path ends in `mesa`.

where-a-file-is-kept.ask: Which of these tells you that a file will still be there after the app stops?
where-a-file-is-kept.answer: It is listed under My Files in the portal
options: It is listed in JupyterLab's file browser
The dot on the notebook's tab has gone
It is listed under My Files in the portal
where-a-file-is-kept.right: The Data Browser reads the Data Store directly, not the running app.

slips.It is listed in JupyterLab's file browse: JupyterLab also lists files on the app's own disk, which is removed when the app ends.
slips.The dot on the notebook's tab has gone: That means the notebook is saved, but not where. It may be on the app's own disk.

where-a-file-is-kept.otherwise: Ask which place shows the Data Store itself.

how-the-app-ended.ask: Your analysis is listed under Canceled, not Completed. Which button ended it?
how-the-app-ended.right: Terminate ends the app at once without saving its outputs.

slips.Save & Exit: Save & Exit stops the app cleanly, and the analysis is then listed under Completed.
slips.Relaunch: Relaunch starts the app again with the same settings. It does not end one.

how-the-app-ended.otherwise: One button stops the app cleanly, and one ends it at once.

pathways.title: New to MESA
pathways.promise: Sign in, start a notebook, and keep what you make.

pathways.title: Get ready for a hands-on session
pathways.promise: Arrive signed in, with an app that starts and the practice data loaded.
pathways.note: Do the first two at least two days before. A new CyVerse account has to ask once for access to apps, and CyVerse says it answers within one to two days. "Ask CyVerse for access to interactive apps", under the first point, shows how.

pathways.title: Check a dataset before you trust it
pathways.promise: Find out what a dataset holds and where it is incomplete or doubtful.

pathways.title: Work in R
pathways.promise: Load the practice data in MESA RStudio Geospatial and check its flags.

pathways.title: Use an AI agent and check what it says
pathways.promise: Test what an AI assistant tells you against the data, then start an agent of your own.

pathways.title: Leave work others can rerun
pathways.promise: Describe your work and leave a notebook that someone else can run again.

p2.title: In R, in MESA RStudio Geospatial
More kinds of table, in R

p4.title: Checks for any result, in R

add-metadata.title: Add metadata to a file or folder
add-metadata.description: Describe a folder in your Data Store with an attribute and a value from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, and confirm the description was saved.
add-metadata.outcome: have a folder that says, in its own metadata, what it contains.

ask-for-a-query-then-run-it.title: Ask an agent for a query, then run it yourself
ask-for-a-query-then-run-it.description: Have an AI agent draft a DuckDB query without running it, read the draft, save it to a file, run it yourself, and write down what the query leaves out.
ask-for-a-query-then-run-it.outcome: have the agent's query in a file beside your notebook, a result you ran yourself, and a note of what the query leaves out.

browse-a-large-folder.title: Browse a large folder as a sorted list
browse-a-large-folder.description: Switch the MESA Portal's Data Browser to a list, page through a folder with many items, and sort what is on the page.
browse-a-large-folder.outcome: have paged through a folder of more than a hundred items, and know what the sort menu does and does not do.

check-a-result-two-ways.title: Check a result a second way
check-a-result-two-ways.description: Compute the same count in pandas and in DuckDB, find out why the two disagree, and keep the result only once both routes give the same answer.
check-a-result-two-ways.outcome: have counted the readings not flagged as suspect in two ways, explained why the counts first differ, and made them agree.

check-a-suggested-result.title: Check an AI-suggested result against the data
check-a-suggested-result.description: Test a result that an AI assistant, or anyone else, hands you: reproduce the number, find what it rests on, and say whether the claim survives.
check-a-suggested-result.outcome: have decided, from the data, whether that claim stands.

check-parts-add-up.title: Check that the parts add up to the whole
check-parts-add-up.description: After splitting a table into groups, add the groups back up and compare with the whole table, so that rows dropped without warning are noticed.
check-parts-add-up.outcome: have caught 150 rows that a grouping dropped without warning, and confirmed a split that loses none.

check-range-and-missing.title: Check a column's range and missing values
check-range-and-missing.description: Find the smallest and largest value in a column and count the blanks in every column, so that an impossible value or a gap shows up before you compute with it.
check-range-and-missing.outcome: know the range of `value` at each gauge and how many blanks each column of `readings` holds.

check-what-an-agent-may-change.title: Check what an agent may change before you let it
check-what-an-agent-may-change.description: Read an AI agent's permission rules in a MESA app, then test them in a scratch folder: what it writes without asking, what it is stopped from, and what a read-only agent does instead.
check-what-an-agent-may-change.outcome: know what your agent changes without asking, what stops it, and how to run it so that it changes nothing.

check-your-usage.title: Check your CPU hours and storage
check-your-usage.description: Find how many CPU hours and how much Data Store space your CyVerse plan allows, and how much you have used, in the MESA Portal.
check-your-usage.outcome: know your plan's limits for computing time and storage, and how much of each is left.

cloud-shell-download.title: Download a file from the web into your Data Store with MESA Cloud Shell
cloud-shell-download.description: Start MESA Cloud Shell, go to a folder in your Data Store, and fetch a file from a web address straight into it with curl.
cloud-shell-download.outcome: have a file from a web address saved in your Data Store.

cloud-shell-keep-running.title: Keep a command running in MESA Cloud Shell after you close the tab
cloud-shell-keep-running.description: Start a slow command in MESA Cloud Shell, open a second terminal window beside it, close the browser tab, and come back from the Analyses page to find the command still running.
cloud-shell-keep-running.outcome: have left a running command, closed the tab, and come back to find it further along.

compare-two-files.title: Compare two files that should look alike
compare-two-files.description: Put July's and August's readings side by side, by row count, by gauge and by largest value, so that what is unusual in one month stands out against the other.
compare-two-files.outcome: have a short list of the places where July's readings and August's differ, each one a question to follow up.

convert-units-before-comparing.title: Bring two units onto one scale before comparing
convert-units-before-comparing.description: Convert readings that were recorded in different units to one unit, using the table that says which unit each gauge reports in, and confirm that every row was converted.
convert-units-before-comparing.outcome: have a `value_mm` column that holds every reading in millimetres, and proof that no row was left unconverted.

count-records-per-day.title: Count records per day to find incomplete days
count-records-per-day.description: Count the rows for each gauge and day to find days that were recorded twice and days that were not recorded at all.
count-records-per-day.outcome: know, for each gauge, whether July has exactly one row per day.

desktop-open-a-file.title: Open a file from your Data Store in a desktop program
desktop-open-a-file.description: Start the MESA KASM Ubuntu Desktop, find a file in your Data Store with its file manager, and open it in a desktop program.
desktop-open-a-file.outcome: have opened an image from your Data Store in GIMP, an image editor, on the MESA desktop.

desktop-open-a-terminal.title: Open a terminal in a Data Store folder on the MESA desktop
desktop-open-a-terminal.description: On the MESA KASM Ubuntu Desktop, go to a folder of your Data Store in the file manager, open a terminal that starts in that folder, and run a command on a file there.
desktop-open-a-terminal.outcome: have a terminal on the MESA desktop, in a folder of your Data Store, that has run a command on a file there.

download-a-file.title: Download a file from your Data Store to your computer
download-a-file.description: Save a copy of a file from the MESA Portal Data Browser to your own computer with the card's Download button, and confirm the copy is complete.
download-a-file.outcome: have a copy of one Data Store file on your own computer, and know it is whole.

find-a-working-group.title: Find a MESA working group and how to join it
find-a-working-group.description: Search the Working Groups page of the MESA Portal, open a group's page, and read what the group is for and who may join, before you ask to join.
find-a-working-group.outcome: know which MESA working groups exist, what one of them is for, and what it asks of people who want to join.

find-community-data.title: Find MESA's community data in the Data Browser
find-community-data.description: Open the MESA community folder in the portal's Data Browser, confirm where you are from the folder header, and copy a folder's path.
find-community-data.outcome: have the MESA community folder open and the path of one of its folders copied, ready to paste into a notebook or a terminal.

find-your-way-around.title: Find your way around the MESA Portal
find-your-way-around.description: Use the MESA Portal's sidebar, dashboard, and user menu to reach your data, the apps, your analyses, and your quota.
find-your-way-around.outcome: know where each part of the portal is, and have checked how much of your quota you have used.

hand-over-and-rerun.title: Hand your folder to a colleague and have them rerun it
hand-over-and-rerun.description: Test whether your work can be repeated without you: share the folder, have a colleague copy it and run the notebook from a fresh start, and compare their result with the one you wrote down.
hand-over-and-rerun.outcome: know whether a colleague can rerun your notebook, without your help, and get your result.

join-and-keep-unmatched.title: Join two tables and keep the unmatched rows visible
join-and-keep-unmatched.description: Join a table of gauges to a table of positions with DuckDB so that a gauge with no match stays in the result and is counted, instead of dropping out unseen.
join-and-keep-unmatched.outcome: have a join in which a gauge with no position is still listed, and a count of how many gauges matched.

keep-an-ai-log.title: Keep a log of AI-assisted steps
keep-an-ai-log.description: Keep a table in your notebook with one row for each step an AI assistant helped with: what you asked, what it answered, how you checked it, and what you decided.
keep-an-ai-log.outcome: have an AI log in your notebook, with a first row filled in.

keep-secrets-out-of-files.title: Keep tokens and passwords out of saved files
keep-secrets-out-of-files.description: Give a notebook a token without typing it into a cell, and confirm that the saved notebook does not contain it.
keep-secrets-out-of-files.outcome: have used a token in a notebook that does not contain it.

launch-jupyterlab.title: Launch MESA JupyterLab with your Data Store mounted
launch-jupyterlab.description: Start the MESA JupyterLab app from the MESA Portal and confirm that your CyVerse Data Store is available inside it.
launch-jupyterlab.outcome: have JupyterLab running in a browser tab, with your CyVerse Data Store files available inside it.

launch-with-options.title: Launch an app with the cores, memory, and time you choose
launch-with-options.description: Start MESA JupyterLab from the MESA Portal with a name, a number of CPU cores, an amount of memory, and a time limit that you set yourself.
launch-with-options.outcome: have MESA JupyterLab running with the resources and the name you chose.

leave-a-rerunnable-notebook.title: Leave a notebook someone else can rerun
leave-a-rerunnable-notebook.description: Restart a notebook and run it from the top, remove what ties it to your session, and say at the top what it needs, so that another person gets the same result.
leave-a-rerunnable-notebook.outcome: have a notebook that runs from a fresh start, top to bottom, without you.

load-a-file.title: Load a file from your Data Store into a notebook
load-a-file.description: Read a CSV file that sits in your Data Store into a pandas table in MESA JupyterLab and confirm its size against what you expected.
load-a-file.outcome: have both practice files loaded as tables in a notebook, with a row count you have checked.

local-days-from-utc.title: Turn UTC timestamps into local days
local-days-from-utc.description: Convert UTC timestamps to local time before grouping by day, and confirm the daily totals against values you already trust.
local-days-from-utc.outcome: have daily rain totals by local day that match the gauge's daily record.

make-a-folder.title: Make a folder in your Data Store
make-a-folder.description: Create a folder in your Data Store from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, so that a piece of work has one place to live.
make-a-folder.outcome: have a new, empty folder of your own in your Data Store.

make-a-new-file.title: Start a new file in the Data Browser
make-a-new-file.description: Create a new file from a template, such as a Markdown note, in a folder of your Data Store with the New File button in the MESA Portal Data Browser.
make-a-new-file.outcome: have a new file in your Data Store, started from a template, ready to open in a MESA app.

map-points-in-rstudio.title: Map point data with sf in MESA RStudio Geospatial
map-points-in-rstudio.description: Turn a table of longitudes and latitudes into spatial points with sf in MESA RStudio Geospatial, check a distance, and save a map to your Data Store.
map-points-in-rstudio.outcome: have a map of the five practice gauges, saved as an image in your Data Store.

monitor-and-extend.title: Check on a running app and give it more time
monitor-and-extend.description: Read how long a running MESA app has left, look at its logs, and extend its time limit from the Analyses page before it stops.
monitor-and-extend.outcome: know how long your app has left, and have given it more time.

move-folders.title: Move folders into another folder
move-folders.description: Select several folders in the MESA Portal's Data Browser and move them together into another folder in your Data Store.
move-folders.outcome: have two folders moved together into a third.

plot-to-spot-odd-values.title: Plot a column to spot odd values
plot-to-spot-odd-values.description: Draw one box per gauge for a column of readings, so that a value far from the rest, or a gauge on a different scale, shows up at a glance.
plot-to-spot-odd-values.outcome: have found one reading and one gauge in `readings` that do not sit with the rest, from a chart.

practice-data.title: Practice data: five invented rain gauges
practice-data.description: The synthetic rain-gauge practice dataset used by the data tutorials: what its five files contain, its data dictionary, and how to copy it into your Data Store.
practice-data.outcome: have the practice files in your Data Store, and know what each one holds.

preview-a-table.title: Look inside a CSV file from the portal
preview-a-table.description: Open a CSV file in the MESA Portal's Data Viewer and read its columns, row count, and value ranges, then run one SQL query, without launching an app.
preview-a-table.outcome: know a table's columns, how many rows it has, and the range of each column, before you launch anything.

query-parquet-with-duckdb.title: Query a Parquet file with DuckDB from a notebook
query-parquet-with-duckdb.description: Run SQL against a Parquet file from a notebook with DuckDB, without loading the file into memory first, and bring a result back as a pandas table.
query-parquet-with-duckdb.outcome: have queried a Parquet file with SQL and turned a result into a pandas table.

r-check-a-result-two-ways.title: Check a result a second way in R
r-check-a-result-two-ways.description: Count the same rows two ways in R, find out why the two disagree, and keep a result only once two independent routes give the same answer.
r-check-a-result-two-ways.outcome: have counted the readings not flagged as suspect in two ways, explained why the counts differ, and reached a total that two routes agree on.

r-check-parts-add-up.title: Check that the parts add up to the whole in R
r-check-parts-add-up.description: After splitting an R data frame into groups, add the groups back up and compare with the whole table, so that rows dropped without warning are noticed.
r-check-parts-add-up.outcome: have caught 150 rows that a tally dropped without warning, and confirmed a split that loses none.

r-check-range-and-missing.title: Check a column's range and missing values in R
r-check-range-and-missing.description: Find the smallest and largest value in a column and count the missing values in every column of an R data frame, so that an impossible value or a gap shows up before you compute with it.
r-check-range-and-missing.outcome: know the range of `value` at each gauge and how many missing values each column of `readings` holds.

r-compare-two-files.title: Compare two files that should look alike in R
r-compare-two-files.description: Put July's and August's readings side by side in R, by row count, by gauge and by largest value, so that what is unusual in one month stands out against the other.
r-compare-two-files.outcome: have a short list of the places where July's readings and August's differ, each one a question to follow up.

r-convert-units-before-comparing.title: Bring two units onto one scale in R
r-convert-units-before-comparing.description: Give each reading its gauge's unit in R, convert every value to millimetres with a lookup you write yourself, and confirm that no row was left unconverted.
r-convert-units-before-comparing.outcome: have a `value_mm` column that holds every reading in millimetres, and proof that no row was left unconverted.

r-count-records-per-day.title: Count records per day in R
r-count-records-per-day.description: Count the rows for each gauge and day in an R data frame to find days recorded twice and days with no record at all.
r-count-records-per-day.outcome: know, for each gauge, whether July has exactly one row per day.

r-hand-over-and-rerun.title: Hand your folder to a colleague and have them rerun it, in R
r-hand-over-and-rerun.description: Test whether your R work can be repeated without you: share the folder, have a colleague copy it and run the script in a new RStudio session, and compare their result with the one you wrote down.
r-hand-over-and-rerun.outcome: know whether a colleague can rerun your script, without your help, and get your result.

r-join-and-keep-unmatched.title: Join two tables in R and keep the unmatched rows visible
r-join-and-keep-unmatched.description: Join a table of gauges to an incomplete table of positions with merge() in R, keep the gauge that finds no match, and count how many matched.
r-join-and-keep-unmatched.outcome: have a join in which a gauge with no position is still listed, and a count of how many gauges matched.

r-leave-a-rerunnable-script.title: Leave an R script someone else can rerun
r-leave-a-rerunnable-script.description: Put your checks in an R script that reads its own data, then run it from an empty workspace in MESA RStudio Geospatial to confirm it does not depend on anything you typed earlier.
r-leave-a-rerunnable-script.outcome: have a script that runs from an empty workspace, top to bottom, without you.

r-load-a-file.title: Load a file from your Data Store in RStudio
r-load-a-file.description: Read a CSV file from your Data Store into an R data frame in MESA RStudio Geospatial, and confirm its size and column types.
r-load-a-file.outcome: have the practice readings loaded as an R data frame, with a row count you have checked.

r-local-days-from-utc.title: Turn UTC timestamps into local days in R
r-local-days-from-utc.description: Read UTC timestamps as times in R, total hourly rain by UTC date and by local date, and confirm that only the local days match the gauge's daily record.
r-local-days-from-utc.outcome: have daily rain totals by local day that match the gauge's daily record.

r-plot-to-spot-odd-values.title: Plot a column to spot odd values in R
r-plot-to-spot-odd-values.description: Draw one box per gauge for a column of readings in R, so that a value far from the rest, or a gauge on a different scale, shows up at a glance.
r-plot-to-spot-odd-values.outcome: have found one reading and one gauge in `readings` that do not sit with the rest, from a chart.

r-query-parquet-with-duckdb.title: Query a Parquet file with DuckDB from R
r-query-parquet-with-duckdb.description: Run SQL against a Parquet file from R with the duckdb package in MESA RStudio Geospatial, and get each result back as an ordinary data frame.
r-query-parquet-with-duckdb.outcome: have queried a Parquet file with SQL from R, and have the result as a data frame.

r-read-the-data-dictionary.title: Read the data dictionary before the data, in R
r-read-the-data-dictionary.description: Use the practice data's dictionary to say what one row of the readings table is, then confirm in R which gauge reports in a different unit.
r-read-the-data-dictionary.outcome: be able to say what one row of `readings.csv` is, and why its `value` column cannot simply be added up across gauges.

r-reconcile-a-join.title: Reconcile row counts before and after a join in R
r-reconcile-a-join.description: Join a data frame of readings to a data frame of gauges with merge() and confirm that the join neither added nor lost rows and left no reading without a match.
r-reconcile-a-join.outcome: have each reading joined to its gauge's name and unit, with row counts that prove the join changed nothing else.

r-record-software-versions.title: Record the R and package versions a result depends on
r-record-software-versions.description: Write the R version and the version of every installed package to files beside your work in MESA RStudio Geospatial, so that a result can be traced to the software that produced it.
r-record-software-versions.outcome: have three small files beside your work that say which R and which package versions it ran on.

r-remove-a-repeated-row.title: Find and remove a repeated row in R
r-remove-a-repeated-row.description: Show the rows of an R data frame that have an exact copy, decide that they are one reading, remove the copy with unique(), and record what you removed.
r-remove-a-repeated-row.outcome: have a table with the repeated row removed, and a note of what you removed and why.

r-save-a-query.title: Save a query from R so someone else can run it
r-save-a-query.description: Write a SQL query to a file of its own from R, then run it from that file with the duckdb package in MESA RStudio Geospatial, so that a colleague runs the same text you did.
r-save-a-query.outcome: have a file, `flagged_readings.sql`, in your practice folder, and one line of R that runs the query from that file.

r-tally-a-quality-flag.title: Tally a quality flag in R
r-tally-a-quality-flag.description: Count the rows for each value of a quality flag in R, including the missing ones, and look at the flagged rows before deciding what to do with them.
r-tally-a-quality-flag.outcome: know how many readings are flagged, which ones, and at which gauges.

r-work-with-a-long-table.title: Work with a long table in R
r-work-with-a-long-table.description: Summarise a long table, with one row per time and per kind of measurement, by measurement in R, and reshape it to one column for each kind with reshape().
r-work-with-a-long-table.outcome: have the hourly observations summarised by measurement and reshaped to one column for each.

r-write-a-readme.title: Write a README for a data folder, from RStudio
r-write-a-readme.description: Add a short README file to a folder in your Data Store, with the editor in MESA RStudio Geospatial, that says what the files are, where they came from, and who to ask.
r-write-a-readme.outcome: have a `README.md` in a folder of your Data Store that describes what is in it.

read-shared-metadata.title: Read the metadata on a folder shared with you
read-shared-metadata.description: Open the metadata on a folder another CyVerse user has shared with you, in the MESA Portal's quick panel and on its full metadata page.
read-shared-metadata.outcome: have read what a collaborator recorded about a folder, and found when it was created and who can reach it.

read-the-data-dictionary.title: Read the data dictionary before the data
read-the-data-dictionary.description: Use a dataset's data dictionary to find out what each column means and which column you cannot yet add up, before you compute anything.
read-the-data-dictionary.outcome: be able to say what one row of `readings.csv` is, and why its `value` column cannot simply be added up across gauges.

read-what-an-agent-ran.title: Read back what an agent ran
read-what-an-agent-ran.description: After an AI agent finishes in a MESA app, list its sessions, export one to a file, and print every tool it called with the inputs it gave.
read-what-an-agent-ran.outcome: have a file with one agent session in it, and a printed list of every tool call in that session.

reconcile-a-join.title: Reconcile row counts before and after a join
reconcile-a-join.description: Join a table of readings to a table of gauges and confirm that the join neither added nor lost rows and left no reading without a match.
reconcile-a-join.outcome: have each reading joined to its gauge's name and unit, with row counts that prove the join changed nothing else.

record-software-versions.title: Record the software versions a result depends on
record-software-versions.description: Write the Python version and the versions of every installed package to files beside your work, so that a result can be traced to the software that produced it.
record-software-versions.outcome: have two small files beside your work that say which Python and which package versions it ran on.

remove-a-repeated-row.title: Find and remove a repeated row
remove-a-repeated-row.description: Find rows that are written twice in a table, decide from what they contain whether one of them can go, remove it, and record what you removed.
remove-a-repeated-row.outcome: have a table with the repeated row removed, and a note of what you removed and why.

rename-a-folder.title: Rename a folder in your Data Store
rename-a-folder.description: Give a folder in your Data Store a clearer name from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, and confirm its path changed with it.
rename-a-folder.outcome: have a folder with a new name, and know what else the change affects.

request-app-access.title: Ask CyVerse for access to interactive apps
request-app-access.description: Send the one-time request that lets a new CyVerse account start MESA JupyterLab and the other interactive apps, and know when it has been granted.
request-app-access.outcome: have asked CyVerse, once, to let your account start interactive apps, and know how to tell when it has said yes.

save-a-query.title: Save a query so someone else can run it
save-a-query.description: Put a SQL query in its own file beside the notebook, with a comment that says what it needs, and run it from that file so that a colleague runs exactly what you ran.
save-a-query.outcome: have a file, `flagged_readings.sql`, beside your notebook, and a cell that runs the query from that file.

save-your-work.title: Save your work where it survives the session
save-your-work.description: Save a notebook inside your Data Store from MESA JupyterLab and confirm from the MESA Portal that it will outlive the app.
save-your-work.outcome: have a notebook saved in your Data Store, and have seen it from the portal.

say-where-data-came-from.title: Say where your input data came from
say-where-data-came-from.description: Record in a folder's README where its data came from, when you retrieved it, which version it is, and what its license allows, so that someone else can get the same data again.
say-where-data-came-from.outcome: have a **Source** section in your README that says where the data came from, when you got it, which version it is, and what its license allows.

search-the-data-browser.title: Search for a file or folder by name
search-the-data-browser.description: Find files and folders by name with the MESA Portal's Data Browser search, narrow the results, and open the folder a result lives in.
search-the-data-browser.outcome: have found a folder in MESA's community data by typing part of its name.

see-an-agents-tools.title: See which tool servers your agent can use
see-an-agents-tools.description: List the tool servers an AI agent has in a MESA app, read which are connected and which need a sign-in, and say what the agent can and cannot reach.
see-an-agents-tools.outcome: know which tool servers your agent has, which are connected, and what each one reaches.

share-a-folder.title: Share a folder with a collaborator
share-a-folder.description: Give one named CyVerse user read access to a folder in your Data Store from the MESA Portal's Data Browser, and confirm the access took effect.
share-a-folder.outcome: have shared one folder, read only, with one person you chose.

share-an-analysis.title: Share an analysis with a collaborator
share-an-analysis.description: Give another CyVerse user read access to one of your analyses from the Analyses page of the MESA Portal, and confirm they are listed.
share-an-analysis.outcome: have one of your analyses shared with a collaborator, who can see it but not change it.

sign-in.title: Sign in to the MESA Portal with a CyVerse account
sign-in.description: Sign in to the MESA Portal at mesa.cyverse.org with a free CyVerse account and confirm that you reached your dashboard.
sign-in.outcome: be signed in to the MESA Portal, looking at your own dashboard.

start-an-ai-agent.title: Sign in and start an AI agent in a MESA app
start-an-ai-agent.description: Sign in to CyVerse from a terminal in a MESA app, connect an AI agent to a language model, and have it list the folders in your Data Store.
start-an-ai-agent.outcome: have an agent that answers a question about your own Data Store.

state-what-ai-did.title: State what AI did in your analysis
state-what-ai-did.description: Add a section to a folder's README that says which AI tools helped with the analysis, what they were asked, what you kept, and how you checked it.
state-what-ai-did.outcome: have an **AI assistance** section in your README that covers every step an assistant helped with.

stop-app-find-results.title: Stop an app and find your results
stop-app-find-results.description: Stop a running MESA app with Save & Exit from the Analyses page and find its results in the Data Browser.
stop-app-find-results.outcome: have stopped a running app cleanly and found the work you saved.

stop-sharing-a-folder.title: Stop sharing a folder
stop-sharing-a-folder.description: Take away a collaborator's access to a folder in your Data Store from the MESA Portal's share dialog, and confirm the folder is private again.
stop-sharing-a-folder.outcome: have removed one person's access to a folder, and seen the folder marked private again.

tally-a-quality-flag.title: Tally a quality flag before you trust a number
tally-a-quality-flag.description: Count how many rows carry each value of a quality flag, including the blanks, and look at the flagged rows before deciding what to do with them.
tally-a-quality-flag.outcome: know how many readings are flagged, which ones, and at which gauges.

trash-and-restore.title: Move a folder to the trash and get it back
trash-and-restore.description: Move a folder to your Data Store trash from the MESA Portal, then restore it from the trash in the CyVerse Discovery Environment.
trash-and-restore.outcome: have put a folder in the trash, and brought it back.

upload-a-file.title: Upload a file from your computer to your Data Store
upload-a-file.description: Copy a file from your own computer into a folder of your CyVerse Data Store with the Upload button in the MESA Portal Data Browser, and confirm it arrived whole.
upload-a-file.outcome: have a file from your computer in your Data Store, where MESA apps can read it.

view-a-notebook.title: Read a notebook in the portal without starting an app
view-a-notebook.description: Open a saved Jupyter notebook in the MESA Portal's Notebook Viewer to read its code and saved output, without launching JupyterLab.
view-a-notebook.outcome: have read a saved notebook, with its output, in the portal.

vscode-find-in-folder.title: Find a value in every file of a folder with MESA VS Code
vscode-find-in-folder.description: Search all the files in a folder of your Data Store for a piece of text in MESA VS Code, read how many times each file contains it, and open a file at the matching line.
vscode-find-in-folder.outcome: know which files in a folder contain a given piece of text, and how many times.

vscode-run-a-script.title: Write and run a Python script in MESA VS Code
vscode-run-a-script.description: Open MESA VS Code on your Data Store, create a Python script in a folder there, and run it in the built-in terminal.
vscode-run-a-script.outcome: have a Python script in your Data Store that reads a data file and prints a result.

work-with-a-long-table.title: Work with a long table, one row per kind of measurement
work-with-a-long-table.description: Recognise a table that stacks several kinds of measurement in one value column, summarise each kind separately, and reshape it to one column per measurement.
work-with-a-long-table.outcome: have the hourly observations summarised by measurement and reshaped to one column for each.

write-a-readme.title: Write a README for a data folder
write-a-readme.description: Add a short README file to a folder in your Data Store, from MESA JupyterLab, that says what the files are, where they came from, and who to ask.
write-a-readme.outcome: have a `README.md` in a folder of your Data Store that describes what is in it.
